hook_text: Two earthquakes in 2010. The bigger one killed about five hundred people. The smaller one killed over a hundred thousand.
clip_script: How is that possible? Chile's earthquake was about five hundred times more powerful than Haiti's. But Chile had strict building laws, steel inside its concrete, and people who had practised what to do. Haiti, the poorest country in the Americas, had weak buildings packed close together right near the epicentre. Earthquakes don't kill people. Buildings do. So engineers put steel braces in walls and giant rubber pads under buildings so the ground can shake underneath. Scientists build warning systems that buy a few precious seconds. And everyone learns three words: drop, cover, hold on. Get down, get under a strong table, and hold on until it stops. Simple. And it saves lives.
visual_style: A whiteboard split screen of Chile and Haiti with death tolls; a building on rubber pads swaying safely; a learner diving under a desk with the words drop, cover, hold on appearing.
pacing: Shock comparison hook, quick explanation, a memorable safety chant.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn how to survive an earthquake.
